_mave.title: Standing with farmers for a resilient future
_mave.description:
Farming communities in the Barind region face growing challenges—from water scarcity and climate uncertainty to limited access to resources and financial support. Yet farmers remain at the heart of food security, environmental stewardship, and rural livelihoods. By standing with them, we can help ensure that those who nurture the land are able to sustain their families and communities with dignity.


Thousands of farmers are already working with CARB to build stronger, more resilient livelihoods—but many more still need support. Every contribution helps expand access to training, water-efficient farming, fair financing, and farmer-centered solutions. By supporting Barind, you are helping farmers grow with confidence, stability, and hope for the future.

_mave.title_en: Other ways you can support us

cards.description_en: Support a small or landless farmer with the resources they need to cultivate their land and secure their livelihood. Your sponsorship helps provide access to seeds, water-efficient farming solutions, training, and guidance—enabling farmers to grow food, sustain their families, and build a more resilient future.

Join hands with Barind to strengthen farming communities across the region. Through partnerships and shared support, we can expand sustainable agriculture, improve access to essential resources, and help farmers adapt to climate challenges while protecting the land they depend on.

data.value: Bangladesh is a pioneer in NGO activities, but few of them include the agriculture sector.

In the drought-prone Barind tract of northwestern Bangladesh, where 75% of the population relies on farming, poor soil, erratic rainfall, and limited water result in low yields. Farmers often turn to local mohazons —moneylenders who can take half of their harvest, perpetuating a cycle of poverty, malnutrition, and lack of social mobility.


To address this issue, Dr. M. Asaduzzaman and local visionaries founded the Centre for Action Research-Barind (CARB) in 1998. CARB aims to free small and marginal farmers, especially borga chashi, from exploitation by offering agriculture-focused microcredit and sustainable farming support.


Over the past 25 years, CARB has worked across Rajshahi, Naogaon, and Chapai Nawabganj, empowering thousands of farmers with tailored financial services, technical assistance, and action-based research. Unlike many microfinance organizations, CARB dared to invest in agriculture—a risk few would take—and proved it can be both impactful and sustainable. Its programs directly improve agricultural productivity, enhance food security, and contribute to Bangladesh’s broader rural economy, where agriculture accounts for 19% of the national GDP.


Today, CARB, with support from its partners, expands its reach, envisioning a future in which farmers have sustainable livelihoods and communities thrive with dignity and opportunity.

_mave.title: The Barind Landscape
_mave.description: The Barind landscape, located in northwestern Bangladesh, is a drought-prone upland area marked by its hard clay soils, unpredictable rainfall, and scarce surface water. It is home to thousands of marginal farming and climate migrant families who grapple with resource constraints, declining groundwater levels, and escalating climate pressures. Agriculture in this region is both vital and precarious—heavily reliant on irrigation and susceptible to ﻿drought, rising temperatures, and soil degradation.

items.altText: Despite these challenges, the Barind is a hub of resilience and innovation. Climate-adaptive farming, water-efficient practices, and community-driven solutions play a crucial role in ensuring livelihoods, food security, and a sustainable future.

Landless and marginal farmers in the Barind region, where over 75% of the population depends on agriculture, face significant hurdles. Many have limited access to credit and often resort to borrowing from local moneylenders who charge exorbitant interest rates—up to 50% of their harvest.

data.value:
Inadequate access to quality inputs and training results in low yields, perpetuating rural poverty that affects more than 21% of the population in northwestern Bangladesh. Excluded from most formal financial systems, these farmers remain vulnerable to cycles of debt, food insecurity, and increasing climate stress.


Barind Tract (or Barind Plains) is situated within the broader Ganges Plain region, specifically forming an elevated terrace within the Bengal Basin. Here, limited surface water and heavy reliance on rice cultivation have led to nearly 2,500 hours of groundwater pumping annually, extracting an estimated 800–1,000 million cubic meters of water to irrigate roughly 500,000 hectares. With rising temperatures and erratic rainfall, groundwater levels in deep tube wells are declining by 0.3–0.5 meters each year. The region’s complex hydrogeology—thick clay layers and fine sand strata—makes aquifer recharge even more difficult.


This ecological stress is the very backdrop of CARB’s existence and mission. Founded in the heart of the Barind, CARB operates as a ground-zero research and action hub—continuously monitoring groundwater, testing regenerative agriculture models, and translating field evidence into innovation. Our goal is long-term ecological sustainability: restoring soil health, reducing water dependence, and building climate-resilient farming systems that protect both farmer livelihoods and the future of the aquifer.

_mave.title: Our Approach
_mave.description:
CARB’s solutions are designed to be flexible, scalable, and transformative for rural farming communities. Its flexibility lies in tailoring services to seasonal demands—whether it’s a small loan for irrigation water, access to drought-resilient seeds, or training on new farming techniques—ensuring every farmer receives what they need, when they need it.


CARB’s strategic framework addresses the complex, interlinked challenges faced by marginalized farmers.


By grounding its approach in action-based research, CARB ensures solutions are evidence-driven and responsive to real needs.


Through locally appropriate projects, it tackles specific environmental, social, and economic barriers, while organizational feasibility guarantees that these interventions remain sustainable, scalable, and impactful over time.

_mave.title: Our Mission
_mave.altDescription: CARB works with people who face a lot of hardships in running their day to day life. Among these people there are landless farmers, farmers with a very scanty amount of lands, agricultural labour’s and people living under poverty line. Very often their lives are dominated by extreme poverty. During the cultivation season they are incapable of buying seeds, fertilizers irrigation water, pesticides etc. As a result they are bound to take loan from moneylenders at a very high rate of interest. After harvest they awfully realize that more than 50% of their crops have been exhausted to repay the loan and its interest. So their permanent companion is poverty and stringency. There is no way out this curse. CARB has come forward to tear this net of curse. CARB sincerely wish to elevate the socio-economic condition of the farmers. CARB is always in search of friends and organizations that are eager to expand their helping hands for the eradication of poverty and elevation of socio-economic status of the poor farmers of Barind tract.

_mave.title: Our Vission
_mave.altDescription:
It wishes the minimization of poverty stringency among the poor, landless cultivators and marginal peasants. CARB dreams of a society which is free from hunger, poverty and the oppression of the local

moneylenders. Its aim is to save the farmers from any sort of interest imposed by well to do moneylenders who encircle the poor by the curse of high rate of interest. The main features of CARB’s activities are the elevation of socio economic condition of the poor farmers, minimization of environmental degradation by massive afforestation, removal of all sorts of exploitation based on age, sex, religion and ethnicity. It also wants the empowerment of female and sex-equality. To achieve its goal CARB invites co-operation from like-minded organization.

_mave.description_en:
CARB’s work is rooted in the belief that farmers themselves must be at the center of solutions to rural poverty and climate vulnerability. Since 1998, CARB has worked closely with Borga Chashi (landless tenant farmers), small and marginal farmers, and climate migrants who move inland from flood-affected chars in search of stability and livelihoods.


We have learned that when farmers are treated not as beneficiaries but as partners—trusted with decision-making, supported with appropriate tools, and organized collectively—their ability to withstand economic and environmental shocks increases significantly.
_mave.description_bn: In contrast, interventions that overlook farmer realities—such as insecure land access, seasonal income cycles, and climate displacement—often fail to deliver lasting change. CARB prioritizes farmer centricity by organizing farmers, strengthening their agency, and ensuring their voices guide program design and implementation.

_mave.description_en:
CARB recognizes that long-term farmer resilience depends on the health of land and water systems. In the drought-prone Barind tract, poor soil, erratic rainfall, and water-intensive cropping patterns have undermined both productivity and environmental sustainability.


Over decades of field-based work, CARB has learned that regenerative and climate-adaptive agriculture is most effective when farmers have access to knowledge, quality inputs, and ongoing support, rather than one-time interventions.
_mave.description_bn: CARB promotes regenerative agriculture as a practical pathway—one that restores soil fertility, reduces pressure on groundwater, and helps farmers adapt to changing climatic conditions while maintaining income security.

_mave.title: What does regenerative agriculture mean at CARB?
_mave.altTitle: Supporting farmers to adopt practices that improve livelihood while protecting natural resources for future generations.

Supporting soil testing, green manuring, fertility management, and training on smart agriculture techniques
Integrating water- saving and conservation practices into everyday farming

_mave.description_en:
Access to safe and reliable water is essential not only for agriculture but also for family well-being, child safety, and social harmony. In rural communities, water scarcity often places a heavy burden on women and children and can lead to conflict, exclusion, and insecurity.


CARB understands that water challenges in the Barind region are deeply interconnected— linking groundwater depletion, irrigation practices, household access, and community relations. Addressing water insecurity, therefore, requires both technical solutions and community-based approaches.
_mave.description_bn: Safe water is not just about cleanliness; it must also be accessible and affordable. CARB ensures that communities can rely on a water supply that meets these criteria, making a significant difference in the lives of the residents by easing access and reducing costs.

_mave.title: What does Safe Water mean at CARB?
_mave.altTitle: Ensuring that families can access clean, reliable, and affordable drinking water without fear, conflict, or exclusion.

infoItems.title: Implementing community-based and household-level equitable access to safe water solutions
Reducing water- related risks for children, girls, and women
Promoting community ownership and cooperation around water usage and management

_mave.description_en:
In the heart of northwestern Bangladesh, about 75% of rural households depend on agriculture for their livelihoods. Yet, many small farmers find themselves excluded from formal financial systems. Traditional credit models often overlook the seasonal nature of farmers' incomes and the unpredictable climate risks they face, forcing them to turn to high-interest informal money lenders and landlords, known as Mohajons and Jamidars.


CARB was born out of a commitment to change this narrative, with a mission centered on agriculture. We offer tailored financial products specifically designed for landless and marginal farmers, aiming to uplift and enhance their way of life. By forgoing physical collateral, CARB embraces group guarantees and social accountability, fostering an environment of trust and responsibility that yields high repayment rates.
_mave.description_bn: Our microfinance offerings are a lifeline, enabling farmers to access vital resources like seeds and fertilizers precisely when they need them. With a repayment schedule that honors the realities of Borga Chashi, small farmers and rural entrepreneurs, we provide a flexible timeline that aligns with their needs. CARB’s adaptable financing turns credit into a tool for bringing stability, empowering the clients to invest in their futures with confidence.

_mave.altTitle: Designing farmer and small entrepreneurship-friendly financial services that reduce dependence on exploitative landlords and moneylenders.

infoItems.title: Providing agriculture- focused microfinance aligned with crop cycles and begin repayment only after harvest
Utilizing community- based guarantees instead of physical collateral, fostering trust and shared commitments
Supporting farmers and small entrepreneurs with credit designed to enable growth, not increase risk

_mave.description_en:
CARB believes that lasting change in agriculture and rural livelihoods requires more than isolated interventions—it must be grounded in evidence, learning, and collective action. From its earliest days, CARB has functioned as a field laboratory, generating root-level, long-term data on groundwater resources, irrigation practices, soil health, cropping systems, and farmer livelihoods across the drought-prone Barind region.


A core pillar of this work is CARB’s targeted, high-impact research on groundwater resource monitoring and irrigation management. Through continuous measurement of groundwater levels, pumping patterns, recharge trends, and irrigation use, CARB builds a deep understanding of how water systems interact with farming practices and climate stress. This evidence allows CARB to design practical, context-specific solutions that promote sustainable water use while protecting farmer livelihoods.
_mave.description_bn: At the same time, CARB recognizes that evidence alone is not enough. For research to translate into lasting impact, it must be amplified through strong coalitions that connect farmers, community institutions, scientists, policymakers, and financial actors. By organizing farmers and building alliances with government agencies, research institutions, and practitioners, CARB transforms grassroots learning into policies and practices that can be adopted at scale.

_mave.altTitle: Turning field-based evidence into collective action that supports farmers and protects natural resources.

infoItems.title: Continuing research on groundwater and irrigation practices to support climate- resilient agriculture and water governance.
Building strong coalitions to amplify grassroots learning and align research with real-world decision-making.
Translating evidence into action by developing practical models and policy recommendations.

data.value: The Centre for Action Research–Barind (CARB) is a grassroots non-profit organization that empowers small and marginal farmers and climate-change-affected families in the drought-prone Barind region, located in northwestern Bangladesh, through agricultural solutions, microfinance, climate-adaptive farming, and action-based research, thereby enabling sustainable livelihoods, food security, and rural resilience.

_mave.title: Building dignified livelihoods and hopeful futures for
Support a farmer today. Help grow livelihoods, hope, and lasting change.
_mave.description:
We believe in thlime strength and potential of every Borga Chashi (landless farmer) and that access to secure resources, fair support, and sustainable livelihoods is key to unlocking that potential. Yet for majority of the Borga Chashi, in the drought-prone Barind region, financial constraints, high land lease costs, and unreliable access to resources make farming a constant struggle. For 25 years, CARB has been working to change this reality.


Through our Sponsor a Farmer initiative, we can support landless farmers with access to land, water-efficient farming solutions, hands-on training, and vital resources—helping them move towards stability, dignity, and hope.


You can be part of this journey. With a monthly contribution of BDT 2500, you can help a farmer sustainably build reliable livelihood sources for their family. Your support helps farmers to leap frog past barriers and create a pathway toward a more resilient and dignified life.

infoItems.title: Research and Advocacy
infoItems.description: Our research is action-oriented, leveraging decades of primary data from the Barind region and advocating for farmer-centric, practical policies and practices, with a focus on improving the future of this historically arid region.

_mave.title: Collaborative Impact
_mave.content: Our collaborations are rooted in trust and shared purpose. We, CARB, bring together farmers, researchers, financiers, and development partners to co-create solutions that strengthen livelihoods, build resilience, and multiply impact beyond what any single actor could achieve alone. By working closely with partners at every level, we unlock new possibilities for impact and long-term resilience.
